# DNS-Shaped Keys: Expanse vs. BTreeMap and QP-Trie

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_readme.py from results/baseline_*.json; do not edit by hand. -->

`ExpanseOrderedBytesMap` against `std::collections::BTreeMap` and [`qp-trie`](https://github.com/sdleffler/qp-trie-rs) `=0.8.2` on domain names stored as reversed-label keys: exact lookup, the predecessor lookup behind a denial-of-existence answer, closest encloser, live heap, and predecessor lookups from concurrent readers. The suite measures the index alone, on synthetic names. Design, arms, pre-registration and claims ceiling: [METHODOLOGY.md](METHODOLOGY.md); tracking issue [#1800](https://github.com/orieg/expanse/issues/1800).

## Provenance

- Dispatch 1 (`baseline_*.json`): 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-12900F (24 threads, 30 MiB L3, Linux 6.8.0-138-generic); core pin `0-15`; governor `performance`; commit `d58eb0dd`; run https://github.com/orieg/expanse/actions/runs/46120661817; 225 load windows, one per harness process; largest busy-CPU figure from outside the run 0.02 core-equivalents.
- Dispatch 2 (`baseline_*_run2.json`): 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-12900F (24 threads, 30 MiB L3, Linux 6.8.0-138-generic); core pin `0-15`; governor `performance`; commit `d58eb0dd`; run https://github.com/orieg/expanse/actions/runs/46122054986; 225 load windows, one per harness process; largest busy-CPU figure from outside the run 0.02 core-equivalents.

## Pre-registered verdicts

Evaluated at n ∈ {100,000, 1,000,000} in both build orders, under METHODOLOGY.md §4 and §5 as amended by A1; the two A2 rows are the predictions of amendment A2, registered after the others were judged and read on their own artifacts. A timing cell is PASS only when its interval lies on the predicted side of the threshold in both dispatches. No result here has had independent review.

## Decision (METHODOLOGY.md §6)

- Winning cell (a PASS on G1, N1 or L1 with no REFUTED cell against `qp_trie` on the same operation): N1.
- A measured advantage to build on (G1 and N1 both PASS): met.
- Ceiling: these synthetic names, these two twin implementations at these versions, one host, single-threaded reads apart from the reader-scaling section. Not a claim about real zones, about B-trees or QP-tries in general, or about a name server's throughput.

## Exact lookup with the probe encoded beforehand (A2)

`expanse_ordered_pre_encoded` reads `expanse_ordered`'s own map with each probe escape-encoded outside the timed window, so the per-lookup encoding pass is removed and the stored key is unchanged (METHODOLOGY.md A2). These are separate runs of `dns_get` with five arms; the table above and G1 to G3 are not drawn from them.

- Dispatch 1 (`baseline_get_a2.json`): 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-12900F (24 threads, 30 MiB L3, Linux 6.8.0-138-generic); core pin `0-15`; governor `performance`; commit `81979942`; run https://github.com/orieg/expanse/actions/runs/46167110825; 45 load windows, one per harness process; largest busy-CPU figure from outside the run 0.02 core-equivalents.

| `sync_reader_get` | 2 | 4.732 | 1.950 [1.946, 1.956] · 1.949 [1.944, 1.952] |
| `sync_reader_get` | 4 | 9.151 | 3.772 [3.761, 3.785] · 3.786 [3.767, 3.794] |
| `sync_reader_get` | 8 | 17.014 | 6.999 [6.986, 7.010] · 6.991 [6.981, 7.001] |

Throughput of `clone_per_reader` over `sync_locked` at W = 8, same workload and pin: 10.889 [10.832, 10.938] · 10.857 [10.803, 10.978]. METHODOLOGY.md §5 reopens an optimistic predecessor only if the lower bound is at least 2 and a caller cannot use snapshots; the suite measures the first condition only.

C3, the control, is REFUTED: the one-shot `get` does not scale under this pin. By METHODOLOGY.md §5, C1 therefore says nothing about the lock. `sync_reader_get` (A1.2) makes the same lookups through a reader each thread registers once; its S(W) rows above show what the per-call registration costs. It carries no prediction.

## Reproduce

```bash
docs/benchmarks/dns_names/run.sh          # full run, on the Linux reference host
docs/benchmarks/dns_names/run.sh --quick  # smoke run into results/quick/ (gitignored)
python3 docs/benchmarks/dns_names/scripts/generate_readme.py
```

On a pull request, `/benchmark dns_names` runs the same runner on the bare-metal host. The harnesses are `crates/expanse/benches/dns_*.rs`; each carries its `# Workload shape` table.
